result: END-seq is an unbiased, high-resolution sequencing method originally developed for mapping double-strand breaks that can be applied to study telomere termini. The method ligates biotin-labeled adaptors to DSBs for purification and NGS sequencing, detecting chromosome ends as unidirectional reads corresponding to the C-rich strand.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm the successful application and validation of END-seq for telomere studies. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'effectively demonstrate the application of END-seq' and 'verify prior data.' Reviewer 2 notes the work 'clearly demonstrates that END-seq can be applied with unprecedented depth and precision.' The editor summarizes that the study 'demonstrates the application of END-seq...concisely demonstrating the utility of this approach.'

result: Telomeres in telomerase-positive cells (HeLa, RPE1) terminate predominantly with the canonical ATC-5' sequence (65-78% of reads), with virtually all reads (99.9%) corresponding to the C-rich strand. This ATC-5' terminal sequence is conserved across mammalian species (human, mouse, dog) and agrees with previous STELA data.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly confirm these findings. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'verify prior data that 5'terminal sequences of telomeres in Hela and RPE cells end in a canonical ATC sequence motif.' Reviewer 2 notes they 'confirm that mammalian telomeres preferentially end with an ATC 5' end.' The editor confirms the authors 'confirm that telomeres in telomerase-positive cells terminate with 5'-ATC.'

result: The canonical ATC-5' terminal sequence bias can be disrupted by T7 exonuclease treatment, which randomizes the 5' telomeric ends. POT1 depletion significantly reduces terminal repeats ending with ATC-5'. Control experiments with pan-centromeric sequences show no similar enrichment or strand bias, validating the specificity of END-seq for telomeres.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these validation experiments without critique. Reviewer 2 states the authors 'confirm...the role of POT1...in regulating telomere termini sequences.' The editor notes the study is 'well-executed and convincing.' These control and perturbation experiments are treated as supporting evidence for the main findings.

result: In mouse embryonic stem cells, POT1a depletion dramatically alters 5' termini (reducing canonical ends from ~70-85% to ~25%), while POT1b depletion has no effect. This demonstrates that POT1a, but not POT1b, plays a dominant role in maintaining proper 5' end processing.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly highlights this as a novel finding, stating 'the authors uncover that POT1b is dispensable for this process. This reveals a novel, important insight relating to the evolution of POT1 as a telomere regulatory factor.' The differential roles of POT1a and POT1b are treated as a significant discovery without any critique.

result: ALT-positive cells maintain the same canonical ATC-5' terminal sequence as telomerase-positive cells (44-57% across three ALT cell lines), with the vast majority of reads (82-98%) corresponding to the C-rich strand. This indicates that terminal 5' end regulation occurs independently of the telomere elongation mechanism.
evaluation: The editor explicitly states the authors 'demonstrate that this principle holds true in telomerase-negative ALT cells as well.' Reviewer 1 confirms they 'verify that the same sequence is present at the 5' ends of telomeres by performing END-seq across a panel of ALT cancer cells.' Reviewer 2 notes they 'demonstrate that, in these cells as well, telomeres frequently end in an ATC 5' sequence.'

result: POT1 depletion in ALT-positive U2OS cells results in formation of 53BP1 foci and dramatically alters the 5' natural termini, demonstrating that POT1 is critical for defining telomere 5' end termini even in ALT cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states 'the established role of POT1...in coordinating the mechanism that maintains the canonical ATC motif is likewise verified' in ALT cells. Reviewer 2 confirms the authors 'demonstrate that, in these cells as well, telomeres frequently end in an ATC 5' sequence via a POT1-dependent mechanism.' No concerns are raised about these findings.

result: Variant telomeric repeats (VTRs) in ALT-positive cells do not occur more frequently than in non-ALT cells within the very terminal portion (first 30 nucleotides) of chromosome ends. However, VTR frequency is higher in internal portions compared to terminal portions (3.8% vs 1.93% in U2OS).
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly requests additional experiments, asking 'are VTRs increased at ssDNA regions of ALT telomeres?' and suggesting 'combining error-free long-read sequencing with END-SEQ to compare the abundance of VTRs within telomeres versus at their distal ends.' The editor notes this as future work 'the reviewers look forward to.' This indicates the VTR findings are incomplete.

result: S1-END-seq reveals that ALT-positive cells contain frequent regions of single-stranded DNA at telomeres, with G-rich and C-rich reads detected at similar frequencies (C/G ratio 0.4-0.58). In contrast, ALT-negative cells show only C-strand reads (C/G ratio 0.98-0.99). This ssDNA presence can distinguish ALT-positive from ALT-negative cells.
evaluation: The editor states 'S1-END-seq is similarly developed for telomeres, showing that ALT cells harbor several regions of ssDNA.' Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'demonstrate that ssDNA abundance is an intrinsic aspect of ALT telomeres.' Reviewer 2 confirms they 'show that ALT telomeres contain single-stranded DNA' and that 'S1-END-seq' can be applied 'to the...accumulation of telomeric single-stranded DNA.'

result: Based on C/G strand ratios, ALT-positive cells contain a minimum of 3-5 distinct single-stranded DNA regions per chromosome end, vastly exceeding the number of chromosome ends. This indicates cells undergoing ALT have multiple ssDNA regions.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly states the authors 'estimate that each telomere in ALT cells harbors at least five regions of ssDNA.' Reviewer 1 confirms the authors 'demonstrate that ssDNA abundance is an intrinsic aspect of ALT telomeres.' The quantitative estimates are accepted without challenge.

result: BLM-deficient U2OS cells show reduced ssDNA levels (C/G ratio 0.7) compared to parental ALT cells. Expression of TRF1-FokI nuclease in BLM-deficient cells induces single-stranded telomeric DNA, restoring the C/G ratio. This demonstrates that ssDNA accumulation is tightly linked to the ALT process and dependent on BLM activity.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states the authors 'demonstrate that ssDNA abundance is an intrinsic aspect of ALT telomeres and is dependent on the activity of BLM, a crucial mediator of ALT.' The BLM experiments are treated as confirming the link between ssDNA and ALT mechanism without any critique.

result: The observed single-stranded telomeric DNA in ALT cells may arise from R-loops, D-loops, internal DNA loops (i-loops), and extrachromosomal circles. These findings align with previous indirect evidence from RPA-staining and native FISH studies suggesting increased telomeric ssDNA in ALT cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 asks the authors to 'speculate if the ssDNA detected in ALT cells might be an intermediate generated during BIR (i.e., is the ssDNA displaced strand during BIR) or a lesion?' Reviewer 3 asks 'To what extent do ECTRs contribute to telomeric ssDNA?' These questions indicate the mechanistic origin and nature of ssDNA remains uncertain and requires further investigation.

result: The regulation of the terminal 5' end of chromosomes occurs independently of the mechanism of telomere elongation, as both ALT and telomerase-positive cells show similar terminal sequence regulation.
evaluation: This conclusion is implicitly supported by reviewers' acceptance of the finding that ALT and non-ALT cells have the same terminal sequences. The editor notes the authors 'demonstrate that this principle holds true in telomerase-negative ALT cells as well,' supporting the independence claim. No reviewer challenges this interpretation.
